newsitem.title: IRAQ: Kurdish fighters take Iraqi town from rivals.
newsitem.headline: Kurdish fighters take Iraqi town from rivals.

text.p: Fighters of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) on Friday overwhelmed a rival Kurdish militia group and seized the strategic northern Iraqi town of Koy Sanjak after heavy fighting, witnesses said.
Guerrillas cheered and waved yellow KDP flags in the streets of the town after PUK forces fled to the nearby Heibet Sultan mountain under a fierce bomardment of artillery and Katyusha rockets.
There did not appear to be many casualties. The KDP's radio station blared out martial music to celebrate the victory.
The fall of Koy Sanjak broke a partial PUK seige of the city of Arbil, northern Iraq's administrative centre that was taken by the KDP fighting with Iraqi government forces in late August.
The United States has urged the two warring Kurdish factions to call an immediate ceasefire.
